judgment.rationale: The two-monitor report clearly distinguishes normal Chrome from saved Chrome PWAs during activation.
evidence: Workspace contains Google Chat, Calendar, and Gmail PWAs.
A normal Chrome window is moved as if it were a saved PWA.
The missing PWA launches over that window.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the incorrect match.

proposed_fixes.title: Match workspace applications by stable PWA identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The existing-window matcher likely falls back to generic Chrome process/title data shared by normal browser windows and PWAs.
plan: Prefer AppUserModelId or shortcut identity and reject generic Chrome for PWA slots.
verification: Activate a workspace with normal Chrome present and confirm it remains untouched while missing PWAs launch.

confidence.rationale: The PWA/browser distinction is explicit; exact fallback code needs confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Workspaces moves an ordinary Chrome window into a PWA slot and launches the missing PWA over it.
known_information: The report uses a two-monitor setup and PowerToys 0.99.1.
Expected behavior is to leave normal Chrome untouched.
inferences: Stable application identity should precede move operations.
issue_context.analysis: The acceptance criterion is preserving unrelated windows, so conservative matching is required.
initial_investigation: Relevant paths are WorkspacesCsharpLibrary/Data/PwaApp.cs, PwaHelper.cs, WorkspaceService.cs, and launcher MainViewModel.cs.
No duplicate, linked PR, or fork fix found.

information_gaps.information: The affected Chrome and PWA versions plus the saved workspace configuration or a short recording showing each window before and after activation.
information_gaps.why_needed: It confirms which PWA identity is available to the matcher and distinguishes an identity fallback from an incorrectly captured workspace record.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the current release, record the Chrome version, launch two saved PWAs and one normal Chrome window, activate the workspace, and attach a short recording or screenshots that show the window titles and positions before and after.

design.root_cause: Generic Chrome matching allows an ordinary browser window to satisfy a saved PWA slot.
evidence: Inferred: matcher lacks stable PWA identity.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: PWA resolution can share a browser executable with normal Chrome.
implementation_steps.change: Expose stable AppUserModelId/shortcut identity and disallow generic-browser fallback for PWA records.
tests: Unit-test PWA and normal Chrome as non-equal.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Candidate may be moved before identity is proven.
implementation_steps.change: Filter candidates through stable identity; otherwise launch the missing PWA.
implementation_steps.code_block:
var match = windows.FirstOrDefault(w => matcher.Matches(w, app));
+if(match is not null) MoveToWorkspace(match); else Launch(app);
edge_cases: Never move a candidate on title alone.
tests: Service test leaves normal Chrome and launches the PWA.

implementation_steps.change: Add it with cleanup and explicit position assertions.

verify: Build Workspaces and run launcher tests.
Reproduce with two monitors, normal Chrome, and three PWAs.
risks: Legacy workspace records may lack identity.
Strict matching may relaunch instead of reuse.
alternatives: Title matching; rejected because titles overlap.
Exclude all Chrome; rejected because browser entries can be valid.

design.title: Protect normal Chrome during workspace activation

actions.label: Request Workspaces PWA identity evidence

comment.body: Thanks for the clear two-monitor reproduction. The behavior indicates that a normal Chrome window can satisfy a saved PWA slot, but the saved identity and capture details are needed to verify the matcher fallback. Please share the Chrome version and a short recording or screenshots from the current release showing two saved PWAs and one normal Chrome window before and after workspace activation, including the relevant window titles and positions.
